strengths: The most premium frame in the set: warm unretouched skin, crisp ivory linen, and the hand's gesture leads the eye straight to the pavé bar and spring ring.

issues: There's no pun. 'Turn it to the front.' is a five-word styling instruction, and the first line ends on 'to' ('Turn it to / the front.').

No visual pun: a plain gift still life with the idea only in the words, the pattern that returned 0.58× in the account.
The opaque cream card covers 14% of the frame, including the box's front-right corner and a petal, and reads as a retail sticker rather than slow luxury.
₹1,499 piece. Low-risk wording: 'closes with a turn, not a catch' is the listing's own line, but the ring is a spring-gate (sailor) ring with a push-pin, which a buyer could call a catch.

strengths: A true visual pun with the piece as the punchline: braided hoops inside an embroidery hoop. 'Hoop in a hoop.' lands in under a second at 390 px.
The correction is plain and true (the brief: a braid of many strands, never a smooth tube), and the price line carries two listing figures, 25 mm and ₹1,499.
Copy on clean blush linen at about 11:1, well clear of the product. Blush, ivory and honey wood on a light ground are exactly on-brand.
issues: ₹1,499 hoops: the data says a single ₹1,499 pair can't pay for ₹1,500–3,000 per sale, so lead with this in a bundle or gift-set offer, not as a solo hero.
'Woven gold strands' uses gold as a colour word (the listing says 18k gold tone). Acceptable, since the product is called Woven Gold Hoops, but never say solid or real gold.
The 23 px price line is about 8 px tall on a phone: legible, but small.
fixes: Optional: ns: 26 (tested: still one line, x 72–832).
